chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams), upon them be peace, who said:
"Whoever drinks wine, even one sip, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty days."
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of drinking wine on one's prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a specific legal ruling (hukm) regarding the consumption of wine (khamr), stating that even a single sip results in the non-acceptance of prayers for forty days. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often interpreted as a temporary spiritual impediment rather than a permanent invalidation of the prayer itself, reflecting the severity of the sin. The narration underscores the direct link between ritual purity and divine acceptance, a key theme in Shia devotional practice.
